fields.title: Over Characteristic Zero, Every Finite Étale Algebra of Rank at Least Three Is a Full Keller Fiber
fields.abstract:
A Keller map can only have finite étale fibers. We ask the reverse question: given a finite étale algebra, can it be made into the whole fiber of such a map? Over a field $K$ of characteristic zero, the answer is yes in every rank at least three. More precisely, for every separable polynomial $P\in K[T]$ of degree $N\geq3$, we construct a polynomial map $F_P:\mathbb{A}^3_K\to\mathbb{A}^3_K$ with $\det DF_P=1$, geometric degree $N$, and a distinguished full fiber naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec} K[T]/(P)$.

The characteristic-zero existence statement also follows by coefficient specialization from the earlier all-degree family of Ulam. We give a quadratic-gauge construction, a scheme-theoretic reconstruction and a formalization of this consequence. The construction is read backwards. A one-variable inverse equation supplies a marked root. Its derivative reconstructs the source and, at the same time, is exactly the factor that cancels from the Jacobian. A translation inserts the prescribed polynomial into this equation. The characteristic-zero theorem, including the automatic translation, function-field comparison, and abstract finite étale corollary, is formalized in Lean. Over a field of characteristic different from $2$, the same formulas also give an explicit supplied-presentation result whenever the first and third Hasse coefficients at the chosen translation are nonzero. That broader result commutes with scalar extension and lies outside the end-to-end Lean formalization. Choices made from an abstract finite étale algebra are noncanonical.
